evidence: Cic. Rep. 5.10: ācer et pugnāx (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 2.19.5: ōrātiō pugnāx et contentiōsa (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Fond of fighting, of soldiers, peoples, cockerels and rams (Petr. 86; Col. 7.3.6); of a speech or a speaker, contentious; in an argument, obstinate (Cic. Pis. 70).
Untamed and bold; in a good sense, spirited and brave (Plautus), but more often overbearing. Cicero gives it to youth: ferōcitās juvenum (Sen. 33).

phrases.latin: nātūrā ferōx, vehemēns, manū prōmptus erat
phrases.english: he was aggressive by nature, violent, quick with his fists (of Cethegus)

sources: Lewis & Short: pugnax · Lewis & Short: ferox
